what: When another program is already listening on port 8765 on all of the computer's addresses, as most servers do, python run.py does not stop with the busy-port message the spec and README promise. It starts anyway, prints that it is running at http://127.0.0.1:8765/, and from then on takes every browser request to that address away from the other program without saying so. The new test cannot see this, because it holds 8765 on 127.0.0.1 alone, the one way of holding the port that does make the start fail. The cause is that the server sets the socket option that allows address reuse (Python's HTTP server does this by default), and on macOS that option lets a bind to 127.0.0.1 succeed beside a program bound to all addresses on the same port. Before this ticket only an explicit --port could reach this; with 8765 as the default it is the plain start's path.
